content:
# 1 Enoch Chapter 106 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 106:2 — Describing Noah's luminous appearance

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "white-as-snow-and-red-as-the-blooming-of-a-rose" | Literal; both similes |
| LOGOS | "white as snow and red as the blooming of a rose" | Formal; preserves both similes |
| PNEUMA | "white as snow and flushed red as a blooming rose" | 'Flushed red' adds color; 'blooming rose' natural |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Blooming of a rose' (EMET/LOGOS) preserves the construct form of the Ge'ez simile. 'Flushed' (PNEUMA) is an interpretive addition for the ruddy skin.

---

## 106:3 — 'lighted up' vs. 'lit up' vs. 'blazed'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he-lighted-up-the-whole-house-like-the-sun" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "he lit up the whole house like the sun" | Formal; natural English |
| PNEUMA | "the light that poured out of them lit up the entire house like sunlight" | Expands source; 'poured out of them' is added |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Lit up the whole house like the sun' is the literal Ge'ez. PNEUMA's 'light that poured out of them' adds a mechanism not present in the source.

---

## 106:4 — 'conversed with' vs. 'spoke with' vs. 'spoke to'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "opened-his-mouth-and-conversed-with-the-Lord-of-righteousness" | 'Conversed' implies dialogue |
| LOGOS | "opened his mouth and spoke with the Lord of Righteousness" | 'Spoke with' preserves the dialogue sense |
| PNEUMA | "opened his mouth — and spoke to the Lord of Righteousness" | 'Spoke to' is unidirectional |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'spoke with.' The Ge'ez suggests mutual communication (dialogue) rather than merely speaking at someone. 'With' preserves this.

---

## 106:6 — 'sons of the God of heaven' vs. 'angels of heaven'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "sons-of-the-God-of-heaven" | Literal: Ge'ez wehib weluda 'Egzi'a Samayat |
| LOGOS | "sons of the God of heaven" | Formal; unusual but literal |
| PNEUMA | "sons of the angels of heaven" | Assumes 'God' should be 'angels' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'sons of the God of heaven.' The Ge'ez reads 'sons of the God of heaven' — this unusual phrase may reflect the Aramaic bene 'elahin (sons of God/angels). The formal rendering preserves the theologically charged ambiguity.

---

## 106:16 — 'giants not according to the spirit, but according to the flesh'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "giants-not-according-to-the-spirit, but-according-to-the-flesh" | Literal; spirit/flesh contrast |
| LOGOS | "giants — not according to the spirit but according to the flesh" | Formal; dash clarifies contrast |
| PNEUMA | "giants — born from flesh, not from spirit" | Inverts order; 'born from' for 'according to' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The spirit/flesh contrast is a theological distinction: the giants derive from the carnal union of angels and humans, not from the spiritual realm. 'According to' preserves the manner-sense better than PNEUMA's 'born from.'

---

## 106:19 — Naming of Noah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "call-his-name-Noah; for-he-shall-be-left-to-you" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "call his name Noah; for he shall be left to you" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Name him Noah. Because Noah will be spared for you" | 'Spared' for 'left'; adds the name for clarity |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Left to you' preserves the Ge'ez verb (yitsar = remain/be left) which contains the etymological wordplay on Noah's name (nuah = rest, but also survival/remaining). PNEUMA's 'spared' captures the meaning but loses the wordplay dimension.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 6**
